title: 3. Innovation and Disruption
subtitle: Wealth management · Robo advisors · DeFi · Big data · Cryptocurrency · Blockchain
subject: FinTech

sections.heading: 3.1 Wealth Management Process
sections.html:
Updated for Assessment Year 2026-27 (income of FY 2025-26, assessed under the Income-tax Act, 1961).

Objectives: explain digital wealth management, DeFi, big data, cryptocurrency and blockchain.

Steps: client profiling → goal setting → asset allocation → portfolio construction → implementation → monitoring and rebalancing. Technology automates profiling, allocation and rebalancing.

sections.heading: 3.2 Platforms, Interfaces and Advantages
sections.html: Platforms such as Groww, Zerodha Coin and ET Money offer mutual funds and stocks through apps connected via APIs to exchanges, AMCs and depositories. Advantages: low cost, convenience, transparency, scalability and 24×7 access.

sections.heading: 3.3 Robo Advisors (Case Study)
sections.html: Robo advisors use algorithms to build and rebalance portfolios from a risk questionnaire. Examples: Betterment, Wealthfront, and in India Scripbox and Kuvera. Fees are typically 0.25–0.5% versus 1–2% for human advisors. Limits: weak handling of complex tax and emotional situations; SEBI's Investment Advisers Regulations apply.

sections.heading: 3.4 Decentralized Finance (DeFi)
sections.html:
DeFi offers lending, borrowing and trading through smart contracts on public blockchains, without intermediaries.

Example: On Aave, a user deposits crypto as collateral and borrows against it automatically.
Risks: smart-contract bugs, volatility, no consumer protection.

sections.heading: 3.5 Social Media Analytics and Big Data
sections.html: Big data is described by the 5 Vs: volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value. Sentiment analysis of social posts helps predict market mood, assess credit risk and tailor products.

sections.heading: 3.6 Cryptocurrency and Blockchain
sections.html:
Cryptocurrency is digital money secured by cryptography. Bitcoin (2009, Satoshi Nakamoto) was the first. Blockchain is a distributed, immutable ledger where blocks are linked by hashes and validated by consensus (Proof of Work, Proof of Stake).

Framework layers: network → consensus → data (blocks, transactions) → smart contracts → application. Tax position for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26): income from the transfer of virtual digital assets is taxed at a flat 30% (plus surcharge and cess) under Section 115BBH, with 1% TDS under Section 194S and no set-off of losses; details are in Module V. Crypto is not legal tender in India.
